groups.title: Tablet (E27500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (558200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, swallowing it quickly.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are on dialysis; if you have high blood magnesium, high blood phosphate, constipation, narrowing of the bowel or acute appendicitis; if you are a woman within the first 3 months of pregnancy; or if the user is a child under 7 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had high blood magnesium or magnesium deficiency; or if you have kidney impairment or have had kidney disease.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a tetracycline antibiotic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with digoxin, captopril, cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine, theophylline, propranolol, atenolol, ferrous sulfate, chlorpromazine, acetylsalicylic acid, naproxen, metoprolol, levodopa, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, ketodeoxycholic acid, sodium fluoride, isoniazid, enoxacin, norfloxacin, levothyroxine, a coumarin derivative, iron or chlorpromazine. Avoid carbonated drinks while taking it.

If diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal distension, skin rash, numbness, phosphate deficiency or, rarely, headache, drowsiness, dizziness or weakness occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Accumulation of aluminium in nerve tissue and bone tissue may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, with or without food. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea; uncommonly vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation, loss of appetite, urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills, purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count, abnormal sensation of the tongue, a change in taste, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm.

groups.title: Oral Solution (D46100ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of the stomach contents (for example after a meal, during pregnancy or with reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 to 20 mL per dose, 4 times in 1 day (after meals and before bedtime).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you must strictly limit sodium, for example because of congestive heart failure or kidney impairment; if you have high blood calcium, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 7 days of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If you take it together with tetracycline, digoxin, a fluoroquinolone, an iron salt, ketoconazole, a neuroleptic, thyroxine, penicillamine, a beta blocker (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), a glucocorticoid, chloroquine, estramustine or a diphosphonate, leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchoconstriction or an anaphylactic reaction occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain and pain from a sprain. This medicine is used for toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day, every 4 to 6 hours when needed. Do not take more than 8 tablets in 1 day. Take it at the lowest dose for the shortest possible period.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment or reduced heart function, or if you have or have had aspirin asthma.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment, kidney impairment or a blood disorder; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have bronchial asthma or impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if a new symptom appears, consult a pharmacist. Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more in adults or 5 days or more in children, and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more. Children and older people should take the smallest necessary amount and watch for adverse reactions.

People who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol must not take this medicine. Do not take it together with another anti-inflammatory analgesic. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take warfarin long term, or if you have taken lithium or a thiazide diuretic.

If signs of shock such as difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema or urticaria, an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function, cyanosis, or hypersensitivity symptoms such as facial swelling, sweating or low blood pressure occur, or if nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (149801ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the treatment of insomnia and for sedation.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (25 mg), 1 time in 1 day, always 30 minutes before sleep. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a breathing disorder such as emphysema, chronic bronchitis or asthma; if you have glaucoma or prostatic hyperplasia; if you are breast-feeding; if the user is a child aged 15 years or younger; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Excessive sedation may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it for 2 weeks or more without consulting a doctor or pharmacist.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with an imipramine-type antidepressant, an anti-Parkinson medicine or disopyramide. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Anticholinergic effects may occur from time to time.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment or cardiac insufficiency; if you have high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you are in early or mid pregnancy, are planning a pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease; if you have risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; if you have had a gastrointestinal ulcer caused by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine in the past; or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

While you are taking this medicine, do not use another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; rhinitis, bronchospasm, peripheral oedema;
